newsitem.title: USA: First Union to buy Signet for $3.2 billion in stock.
newsitem.headline: First Union to buy Signet for $3.2 billion in stock.

text.p: First Union Corp. said Monday it will acquire Signet Banking Corp. for about $3.2 billion in stock in a deal that will create the biggest bank in Virginia and the No. 2 bank in greater Washington, D.C.

Industry analysts said the deal was expensive but could prove worth it for First Union, which they said was defending part of its territory after rival Wachovia Corp. agreed to buy two banks based in Virginia, Central Fidelity Banks Inc. for $2.3 billion and Jefferson Bankshares Inc. for about $540 million.

"There is no question that the price is expensive," said Moshe Orenbuch, analyst at brokerage Sanford C. Bernstein Co. He noted First Union is paying about 3.4 times book value, very high by historical standands, but added, "The reality is that they can make the numbers work."
Banks have been merging at a rapid clip as they seek to grow by expanding into new markets.
The combined company, which will keep the First Union name, will have about $155 billion in assets and 2.2 million customers in Virginia, Maryland and the District of Columbia.
In addition to being the biggest bank in Virginia, the combined company will rank second in the Washington area, where First Union is currently fourth largest.

"The strong presence Signet has established in Richmond, Baltimore and Hampton Roads is a perfect fit for First Union's leading presence in Roanoke and our strong market position in Washington, D.C.," First Union Chairman Edward Crutchfield said in a statement.
First Union is the nation's sixth largest bank, with operations from Florida to Connecticut. Signet, based in Richmond, Va., is the No. 50 banking company ranked by assets.
Nancy Bush at brokerage Brown Brothers Harriman said the deal looked "defensive" for First Union, given the recent moves by rival Wachovia, which is based in Winston-Salem, N.C.

First Union, based in Charlotte, N.C., said it would save about half of Signet's annual expenses after the merger, or $242 million, and that it expected the acquisition to enhance its earnings starting next year.

Under the deal, First Union will offer 0.55 of its shares for each Signet share, valuing Signet at about $52.25 a share based on Monday's market price and before adjusting for First Union's previously announced 2-for-1 stock split payable July 31.
Signet stock jumped $14 to $50.69 while First Union stock fell $2.44 to $95, both in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
First Union also said it expected to take a charge of $135 million this year to cover one-time, merger-related costs.

Following the merger, Signet Chairman Malcolm McDonald will become chief executive officer of First Union's Virginia, Maryland and Washington region. Benjamin Jenkins III, current president of First Union's operations in the region, will become chief operating officer.
Under the deal, Signet granted First Union an option to buy up to 19.9 percent of Signet's stock.
The merger is subject to approval by Signet shareholders and regulators and is expected to close by Dec. 31, the companies said.

First Union Vice Chairman John Georgius said on the CNBC cable television business channel that if regulators require any asset sales or divestitures for the deal to be completed, he believes they would be minimal.

Asked about other mergers, Georgius said the banking industry was consolidating and First Union has an "open mind" about "good opportunities at the right price," noting First Union's strength is along the East Coast.
